A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProFS research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–H. Content can be matched reliably across pagination changes and table renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original toxicity-reduction, model-capability, sample-efficiency, robustness and alignment experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and additionally reports a KTO comparison and benign-prompt generation examples.

M1.justification: The three-step ProFS procedure remains unchanged: remove the corpus-mean direction, identify a toxic subspace using SVD, and project MLP weights away from it. Equations (1)–(3) and Algorithm 1 retain the same operations.

E1.justification: v5 adds benign-use scenarios involving toxic vocabulary, including etymological and educational requests (Table 16). All named datasets remain unchanged. The malicious Wi-Fi and phishing examples in new Table 15 already appeared in v4 Tables 16 and 15.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds KTO alongside the retained DPO, DexPerts and Toxification Reversal comparators. KTO has a reported result, rather than merely a citation, although Appendix F.2 and detailed Table 13 are not expanded to include it.

E3.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a qualitative probing design contrasting harmful intent without toxic vocabulary against benign uses of toxic vocabulary. It combines existing HH-Golden-aligned examples with new toxicity-aligned Mistral-7B probes. Retained benchmark splits, metrics, model sizes and sample budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new 'Robustness to Toxic Prompts' analysis examines whether editing merely suppresses words or prevents benign discussion of related concepts. It combines reused malicious-prompt examples with two new benign examples. Existing centering, layer-selection, label-noise and sample-selection analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-run mean and standard-deviation reporting and existing uncertainty displays. The added KTO row follows Table 3's existing point-estimate format; no new seed, repeated-run or statistical-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v5 adds KTO's 41.13% toxicity result and qualitative comparison indicators in Table 3, plus two benign-prompt continuations in Table 16. Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged, including Table 4's 74.1% DPO and 78.2% ProFS win rates. Redisplayed malicious examples are not new outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (4) and (11) replace unindexed corpus-mean coefficients a+ and a- with sample-indexed coefficients a_i+ and a_i-, propagated through the centering and gradient expressions. This modestly generalizes the written factor model to sample-specific loadings. The recovery bound and remaining theoretical arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain sample-efficient, noise-robust, tuning-free editing and a connection to a denoised DPO step. Section 9 now says 'unwanted behaviors' rather than 'model toxicity', but broader preference alignment was already claimed and evaluated in v4 Sections 7 and H.

C2.justification: New Appendix F.1 interprets the examples as showing recognition of malicious intent, refusal without explicit refusal alignment, and retained knowledge for benign discussion. These interpretations were previously absent. The existing limitations concerning singular-vector selection and restriction to MLP layers remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation recipes, rank and layer settings, DPO/LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, compute accounting and code/data access information are retained. The new KTO result is not accompanied by KTO-specific implementation or training details.

R1.justification: v5 adds Ethayarajh et al. on KTO, Bajaj et al., Syamkumar et al., and two Uppaal et al. references, while removing Hammarling's SVD reference. These are limited citation additions and a removal; the main positioning relative to editing and tuning remains intact.

P1.justification: v5 copyedits several passages, trims introductory repetition, condenses and rearranges Section 9, adds acknowledgments and the robustness paragraph, and changes the publication header. The overall section structure and narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: v5 restyles Figure 1, adds metric-direction arrows and a KTO row, and introduces Tables 15–16, with Table 15 redisplaying existing examples. Several retained figures and tables move, and subsequent tables are renumbered. Existing plotted results are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added KTO comparison and benign-vocabulary examples modestly broaden the evidence, while copyediting improves clarity. These gains are limited: KTO lacks supporting setup details, and the new refusal interpretation overstates an ambiguous phishing response. The additions improve coverage without resolving a major deficiency; the core method and established results remain unchanged.
